candidates.title: Beach Plum Island: Delaware's only 'wilderness beach'
candidates.whyHeld: Beach Plum Island already ran as Hidden Gem on 2026-07-15; Thompson Island is the current gem as of 2026-08-11. Re-running it would show readers the same selection four weeks later. This research is materially richer than the July entry — fees, closures, permits, access rules — so it is preserved for a standalone feature.

research.name: Beach Plum Island Nature Preserve
research.location: South Bayshore Drive, north of Lewes via Route 1 to Broadkill Road (Route 16)
research.access: Open daily, 8 a.m. to sunset, March 1–December 31. Access restricted to marked hiking trails and state-designated fishing areas; the southern half of the preserve is closed to all access year-round.
research.parking: On-site parking; administratively part of Cape Henlopen State Park but physically separate, reached via South Bayshore Drive.
research.trailDetails: A roughly two-mile undeveloped barrier spit with a northern-half trail system used for hiking, beachcombing, wildlife viewing, and surf fishing along the Broadkill River and Delaware Bay shoreline.
research.seasonalLimitations: Closed December–February; insect repellent recommended in warmer months.
research.closures: Southern half of the preserve is permanently closed to protect the barrier dune system and its wildlife.
research.rules: Stay on marked trails and designated fishing areas; this is a dedicated state nature preserve, not a general-use beach.
research.practicalDetail: Delaware State Parks' official 2026 rate sheet lists a daily entrance fee at ocean parks (which includes Beach Plum Island) of $10 for Delaware-registered vehicles and $20 for out-of-state vehicles, charged March 1–November 30. A vehicle surf-fishing permit (separate from the entrance fee) is required for 4WD beach access; per DNREC's 2026 season announcement, reservations are no longer required for surf-fishing access at Beach Plum Island specifically, though the underlying annual/off-peak permit is still required.
research.whyItMatters: Dedicated a State Nature Preserve in 1990, it's described by Delaware's own tourism byway program as the only 'wilderness beach' left in the state park system — undeveloped, uncrowded, and protecting a barrier-spit ecosystem of beach, dune, tidal marsh, and river habitat.

relatedReviewNotes: Long-form opportunity: Beach Plum Island's designation as the state park system's only 'wilderness beach' could support a dedicated nature/ecology feature beyond this week's Hidden Gem slot.
